editorial:
Imagine a guy who thinks he is too cool for everyone. That is Eugene Onegin. He is a rich, bored young man who heads to the country and meets Tatyana, a shy girl who loves reading books. She falls head over heels for him and tells him everything in a sweet letter, but he just brushes her off. He tells her he is not the marrying type and basically breaks her heart. The whole vibe is very fancy, with beautiful costumes and great music from Tchaikovsky that makes you feel like you are actually in old Russia.

You will love how the roles flip later in the story. The acting is solid, and the music really carries the emotion when the characters cannot find the right words. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the drama makes up for it. If you like stories about missed chances and regret, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Years later, Onegin sees Tatyana again, but she is now a powerful and elegant woman married to a prince. Now he is the one in love, and he begs her to leave her husband for him. Tatyana still loves him, but she refuses because she wants to be honest and loyal to her marriage. She tells him goodbye, leaving Onegin alone and heartbroken, realizing he threw away the only real love he ever had.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tragic romances and classical music.
